findings.title: Six relied-on deliverables lack the required immutable SHA-256 digest
findings.criterion_ref: Criteria 6 and 7.3: the checkpoint must provide an immutable digest for every deliverable it relies on, specifically a final sha256 under criterion 7.3.
findings.trigger: The submitted checkpoint relies on checkpoint_digest.json, digest_manifest.json, and the four evidence/ledger files, while digest_manifest.json explicitly excludes all six and no other published SHA-256 manifest covers them.
findings.consequence: Those evidence and binding files can be changed without violating any published deliverable SHA-256, so the gate cannot establish the immutable, fully digest-bound evidence set required by criteria 6 and 7.3.
findings.evidence: Section 2.4 says the excluded files are covered by a checkpoint tree id, but the opening identity section and evidence/checkpoint_digest.json explicitly say no tree id is published. evidence/digest_manifest.json lists the six paths in excluded_paths. The four ledger files have blank sha256_now fields in evidence/ledger/path_ledger_complete.json, and evidence/ledger/delta_raw_with_blob_shas.txt expressly omits the four ledger files. Only the report and digest_manifest SHA-256 values are published in evidence/checkpoint_digest.json.

observations: The report says digest_manifest.json covers “218 other deliverables,” while the manifest’s covered_count is 230; the actual manifest entries re-hashed successfully, so this appears to be a stale narrative count rather than an additional blocker.

The live git status has 238 lines versus 237 in the frozen status evidence because the current gate-created QA/ directory is untracked. The checkpoint explicitly discloses QA/ as gate-owned post-freeze state, so I did not treat that expected gate mutation as a finding.
reasoning: The checkpoint and digest-manifest anchor hashes match the submitted values, all 230 hashes inside the manifest verify, the pre-move journal ordering is ACT-039/040 before ACT-041/042, and the report supplies substantial evidence for the move and tests. However, the immutable-coverage requirement is absolute at this threshold: six relied-on deliverables are deliberately excluded without the claimed fallback tree digest. Because criterion 7.3 expressly requires SHA-256 coverage of every relied-on deliverable, this survives as a blocker.
